title: Tail-latency lab notes — Llama/Mistral/Qwen + MoE routing
content:
Summary:

This note captures lab work looking for root causes of intermittent tail-latency spikes observed when serving long-context workloads across three model families (Llama, Mistral, Qwen) and mixed MoE topologies. The behaviour is sporadic: median latency is stable but p99 shows 2x–6x spikes under realistic traffic. Aim: enumerate hypotheses, reproducible micro-benchmarks, and quick mitigations.

Quick findings (TL;DR):
- Two dominant classes of events: scheduling-induced microbursts in MoE routing (expert handover hotspots) and memory-path/IO stalls (UVM page faults or PCIe DMA stalls) in certain Qwen + long-context configs.
- Llama workloads show more gradual degradation (KV-eviction churn), Mistral exhibits short compute spikes due to attention kernel divergence for >16k windows.
- Reproducible local test that triggers p99 spike: fanout=4 MoE with skewed token distribution (session-skew) + batch coalescing window of 60ms.

Experimental setup / notes:
- Hardware: 8x A100 (40GB) per node with NVLink, PCIe Gen4 host, kernel 6.1 (internal perf kernel).
- Runtime: prod-edge build 2024-10-29 (commit a2e6f3), with continuous-batching enabled, prefix/KV cache on by default.
- Bench harness: synthetic traces derived from production logs (seeded session lengths 512/2048/8192), repo scripts: scripts/bench/tail_latency_sweep.py (linked in PR).
- Instrumentation: trace shards collected with jaeger + local per-request microtrace (timestamps at: accept, route, prefetch_submit, kernel_launch, dma_start, dma_end, kv_load, kv_evict, finish). Additional metrics from nvprof-style counters: SM_active_pct, SM_stall_mem, pci_dma_latency_ms, uvm_page_faults, gpu_mem_util, interconnect_bw

Representative run (repro):
- Config: MoE model (2-expert-per-token), fanout=2, batch-window=60ms, coalescing=on, request mix: 30% long (8k tokens), 70% short (128 tokens).
- Observed: p50=83ms, p95=162ms, p99=640ms.
- Trace pattern for p99 traces: normal flow until the router step; router emits 2x parallel expert requests; one expert returns quickly, the other stalls at 'dma_start' for ~420ms then completes; overall request waits.
- Kernel counters during stall: SM_active_pct=12%, SM_stall_mem=78%, pci_dma_latency_ms median=14ms but with outliers >300ms aligning to stalls. uvm_page_faults spikes correlate with the worst traces (3–8 page faults/request).

Hypotheses and evidence:
1) MoE scheduling + coalescing race: under skewed session distribution, the runtime coalesces token fragments into a batch that maps unevenly to expert shards; locking and handovers cause one expert's dispatch to be serialized leading to head-of-line blocking. Evidence: profiles show routing enqueue timestamp variance large (>200ms) between experts for same request. A quick mitigation (disable coalescing for MoE_fanout>1) reduces p99 by ~45% in lab.

2) UVM/Host->GPU path instability with large KV windows (Qwen long-context): when model maintains large KV caches across many sessions, eviction/restore causes page faults during DMA which stalls kernels. Evidence: uvm_page_faults counter up during experiments and PCIe DMA latency outliers. Workaround: pin KV shards to device memory for hot sessions (trade memory for stability) reduced page faults to near-zero for targeted sessions.

3) Attention kernel divergence on Mistral for >16k: certain attention tiling code paths get triggered causing extra kernel launches and temporary serialization (small kernel launches with high kernel launch latency). Evidence: trace shows a burst of short-lived kernels in the attention phase with high cumulative launch overhead. Patch candidate: merge small attention kernels when seq_len > threshold (proof-of-concept +12% p99 improvement in microbench).

Repro recipes (how to provoke locally):
- MoE microburst script (shell):
  python scripts/bench/tail_latency_sweep.py --model moe-skew --fanout 2 --batch-window 60 --traffic-mix skewed
- KV-page fault stress (Qwen): start many sessions with long prefix followed by random access patterns to force evictions:
  python scripts/bench/kv_eviction_stress.py --model qwen-32k --sessions 200 --prefix-size 8000 --evict-rate 0.7
- Profiling flags: RUNTIME_TRACE=1 ENABLE_UVM_METRICS=1 PERF_SAMPLING=off

Detailed trace excerpt (one p99 event):
- t=0 accept
- t=2 route start
- t=6 router enqueue expert_A (fast)
- t=7 router enqueue expert_B (slow)
- t=30 prefetch_submit
- t=35 kernel_launch expert_A -> complete at t=120
- t=120 dma_start expert_B -> dma stalls until t=560 (u v m pagefault handler calls at t=240, t=360)
- t=560 kernel_restart expert_B -> complete at t=640
- finish at t=642

Root causes summary (actionable):
- Short-term mitigations (fast to deploy):
  * Disable coalescing for MoE when fanout>1 and session_skew metric > 0.6 (feature-flag controlled). Owner: Marco Silva.
  * Add uvm_page_fault backpressure counter to router heuristics: if faults/sec per-GPU > threshold, throttle inflight long sessions. Owner: Priya Natarajan.
  * Increase attention kernel fuse threshold for Mistral builds in runtime. Owner: Ethan Brooks.

- Medium-term fixes (engineering work):
  * Router: upgrade handoff protocol to use optimistic per-expert queues and prefetch reservations (design doc started, INF-2793).
  * Memory manager: better hot-session pinning heuristic + TTL-based pin eviction to reduce UVM churn.
  * Kernel scheduler: batch small attention kernels together when seq_len window triggers fragmentation.

Follow-ups / TODOs:
- (Ava) Run a 24h canary with coalescing disabled for MoE traffic slices (canary config queued).
- (Marco) Implement a low-overhead router enqueue histogram and alert on skew in prod metrics (JIRA INF-2793).
- (Priya) Add nightly stress job for UVM page-fault reproduction and attach traces to JIRA.
- (Ethan) Prototype attention kernel fusion patch and run microbench across Mistral/LLM variants.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Why do some GPUs show far worse pci_dma_latency outliers than identical peers in the same rack? (hardware vs driver vs workload locality?)
- How do cloud NIC interrupts and host CPU steal interact with router serialization? Need host-level trace correlation.

Notes-to-self / rough next experiments:
- Correlate exact host CPU load / IRQ counts with stalls; capture perf top across the host when reproducing.
- Test MoE with experimental optimistic handoff (local patch) under synthetic skew to quantify worst-case queueing.
- Add a synthetic 'fake_page_fault' injector in the UVM shim to see routing responses to synchronous page faults (safe lab only).

References:
- github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/418 (bench harness, stress scripts)
- JIRA INF-2793 router handoff design
- confluence/redwood/serving-runtime/tail-latency-playbook (placeholder for final runbook)

Appendix (raw numbers from a stable reproduce run):
- config: 8k-long tokens, fanout=2, batch-window=60ms, 200 qps sustained for 10 minutes
- measured: p50=83ms, p90=145ms, p95=162ms, p99=640ms, max=1.2s
- uvm_page_faults: avg 0.12/s per-GPU, during spike window up to 6.8/s
- pci_dma_latency: median 12ms, worst 420ms (correlates to p99 traces)

If you're reviewing: please flag any other quick-check experiments you want added to the runbook. This is intentionally lab-focused — will convert to a playbook after one-cycle of canary results.
